definitions.explanation: Chinese-style cooking, especially as adapted and enjoyed in Japan. Often used as a prefix for Chinese food items.
Relating to China or Chinese culture more broadly, though the food-related sense is by far the most common in daily use.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{中華|ちゅうか}を{食|た}べよう。
{駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しい{中華|ちゅうか}レストランができた。
examples.english: A new Chinese restaurant opened in front of the station.

examples.japanese: この{中華|ちゅうか}{料理|りょうり}{店|てん}の{麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}は{本場|ほんば}の{味|あじ}に{近|ちか}い。
examples.english: The mapo tofu at this Chinese restaurant tastes close to the authentic version.

examples.japanese: {中華|ちゅうか}{人民|じんみん}{共和国|きょうわこく}
{中華|ちゅうか}{圏|けん}では{旧正月|きゅうしょうがつ}を{盛大|せいだい}に{祝|いわ}う。
examples.english: In the Chinese cultural sphere, the Lunar New Year is celebrated grandly.

examples.japanese: {中華|ちゅうか}{思想|しそう}は{東|ひがし}アジアの{歴史|れきし}に{深|ふか}い{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: Sinocentric thought had a deep influence on East Asian history.

notes:
{中華|ちゅうか} most commonly refers to Chinese cuisine in everyday conversation.

COMMON FOOD COMPOUNDS:
- {中華|ちゅうか}{料理|りょうり} (Chinese cuisine)
- {中華|ちゅうか}{鍋|なべ} (Chinese-style wok; Chinese hot pot)
- {中華|ちゅうか}そば (Chinese-style noodles, ramen)
- {中華|ちゅうか}{丼|どん} (Chinese rice bowl)
- {中華|ちゅうか}{街|がい} (Chinatown)
- {中華|ちゅうか}まん (Chinese steamed bun)

In Japan, {中華|ちゅうか}{料理|りょうり} often refers to Chinese food that has been adapted to Japanese tastes, while {中国|ちゅうごく}{料理|りょうり} may refer to more authentic Chinese cuisine.
